about.title: Plymouth Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Plymouth is a small place, roughly 1,070 residents in Amador County, and when someone here dies because of another person's carelessness, the whole town tends to feel it. In the most recent final crash year, 2025, public records list zero traffic deaths inside city limits. That is good news, but it also means a fatal wreck on Route 49, Shenandoah Road, Miller Way or Empire Street would be an exception rather than a pattern, and families are rarely prepared for what follows. Wrongful death claims in California are not limited to car crashes, either; they can grow out of a fall on someone else's property, a workplace incident, a defective product, or medical care that went wrong. LawProactive does not practice law. We are a free service that listens to what happened and connects you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You decide whether and when to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Plymouth Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits who can bring a wrongful death action: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year clock does not pause for grief
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity may be responsible. Connecting early keeps those options open.

items.title: A civil claim that stands on its own
items.desc: A wrongful death case is separate from any criminal proceeding and can recover funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on Route 49 near Plymouth. Does the location change anything?
items.answer: It can. When a state highway or other public roadway is involved and a government entity might share responsibility, California requires a formal claim to be presented on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney soon, even if you are not ready to make decisions. LawProactive can connect you at no cost so those deadlines are understood early.

items.question: Plymouth recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that make a wrongful death claim less likely to be taken seriously?
items.answer: No. A claim is judged on what happened in your loved one's case, not on how often similar deaths occur in town. Wrongful death actions also cover far more than traffic collisions, including falls, workplace incidents, defective products and medical negligence. The independent attorney you are connected with will look at the specific facts, not the local averages.

items.question: There is already a criminal investigation. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: You do not. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil matter with its own standards and its own timeline, and it can move forward regardless of whether criminal charges are filed or how they turn out. Many families find it helpful to have an attorney involved while evidence is still fresh. Waiting for a criminal case to conclude can eat into the two-year filing period.
